renderedGroups.speaker: Narrator
renderedGroups.text: Section 2 You will hear the director of a club giving

renderedGroups.speaker: Narrator
renderedGroups.text: a talk about an ancient game played on ice called curling.

renderedGroups.speaker: Narrator
renderedGroups.text: First you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16 on page 4.

renderedGroups.speaker: Narrator
renderedGroups.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: It gives me great pleasure to welcome you to the Montreal Curling Club.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: I hope you'll enjoy the introductory program we've prepared for you.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: I'll start with a brief introduction to the game itself and the equipment,

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: so that you'll be able to enjoy it when you watch it later on.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: I'll then go on to say a little about the history of the sport and the club.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: So, first let's take a look at the game of curling and the implements it uses.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: It's played on ice, and the object of the game is for two teams to push heavy stones

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: across the ice towards a target.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: Now there are four people in each of the two teams.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: The first is called the lead.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: The next is called the second.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: The next, surprise surprise, is called the third.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: and the final player, who is absolutely key, functions as the captain, but is

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: always called the skip. That's S-K-I-P. The area of play on the ice, whether it

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: be on a rink or on a frozen lake or a stream, is called the sheet. This long

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: thin area is 42.15 meters by only 4.25 meters, and unlike ice hockey ice, for

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: example, it is constantly groomed by frequent shaving to keep it perfectly

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: level. At either end of this are the two zones for the targets. Each one is known

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: as a house. A little bit about the equipment we need. The stones are made

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: from granite. Originally these were held by your fingers in holes specially carved out in the top,

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: but then it was decided to add a handle to get a better grip.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: The other distinctive implement is the brush or broom. This is used for two purposes,

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: to clean the ice of course, but more crucially to warm it. This melts the ice slightly and

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: lessens the friction, so you get a smoother slide.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: Curling is not an expensive sport.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: You don't buy your own stones.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: In fact, it is illegal to play in a match with your own stones.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: But you can use your own brush.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: There are two main types, Scottish and Canadian.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: The former are normally made out of horse hair, and the latter, which are now more

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: frequently used are made of synthetic materials, and they don't leave as many threads on the

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: ice.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: Now, apart from stones and brushes, the only other piece of equipment you would need as

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: a beginner is a rubber sole on one of your shoes, depending on which shoe you LEAD from.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: The captain will often carry a stopwatch to gauge when the ice needs to be changed.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: All equipment and clothing can be bought in the club shop.

renderedGroups.speaker: Narrator
renderedGroups.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20 on page

renderedGroups.speaker: Narrator
renderedGroups.text: 4. Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: A quick word about Montreal Curling Club,

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: it's renowned. Not only because it often wins championships, but because it was the first club

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: for any sport in the whole of the North American continent.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: And although curling is not as well known as many other winter sports, we still boast

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: a certain amount of influence in the National Sports Council.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: And what are the origins of the game?

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: It's now well established that it started in Scotland in at least as early as the 16th

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: Queen Victoria, on her frequent trips to Scotland, often played it, but wrote in her diary that

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: it required exceptional strength to throw the stones. Her patronage attracted a great

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: deal of interest in the game, especially amongst younger players, and this was enhanced

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: further when she granted a royal title to the Caledonian Curling Club, which had been

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: set up in the early 19th century to create standard rules for the game.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: Curling has always had support in high places.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: In the 16th century, the Scottish Parliament actually banned golf and football as violent

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: and unprofitable sports.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: They felt that local men should spend any free time practicing archery for self-defense

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: against their enemies.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: But the less popular game of curling wasn't included in the ban.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: The art of throwing stones was thought to be just as useful as shooting arrows.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: But back to Canada.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: Here the game has flourished since the beginning of the 19th century,

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: when Scottish soldiers posted there enjoyed playing it on the frozen lakes and rivers.

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: Because of the difficulty in importing granite stones from Scotland,

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: cast iron was used instead, obtained from melted-down cannonballs which had

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: originally been brought over from Europe. Now Canada is regarded as the most

renderedGroups.speaker: Club director
renderedGroups.text: successful curling nation in the world. Now, the game you're going to see.
